title: Gas Fired Furnace
model_title: Gas-Fired Process Heater (Box Type: Radiant + Convection Sections)

introduction.definition: A gas-fired process heater (furnace) heats a process fluid flowing through tubes. Burners fire into a refractory-lined radiant box; tubes along the walls absorb radiant heat. The flue gas then flows up through a convection section, where more tubes recover heat, and leaves by the stack. A damper controls the draught.
applications: Crude and vacuum heaters in refineries
key_points: Convection section recovers heat from cooler gas
Draught and excess air control efficiency and safety

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Efficiency vs excess air: too little → CO and unburnt fuel; too much → heat lost in the stack. Typical target O₂ ~ 2–3 % (gas).

temperature.title: Flue-gas temperature: radiant → convection → stack
temperature.description: Most heat (often ~ 60–70 %) is absorbed in the radiant section, where the flue gas is hottest (bridge-wall temperature often ~ 700–900 °C). The convection section recovers more heat from the cooler gas; the stack temperature sets the main efficiency loss. Tube metal temperature and heat flux limit the firing rate (API 560 / API 530).

foundation: Foundations designed for heater weight and thermal growth; refractory dry-out schedule after installation.
alignment: Burner alignment so flames do not impinge on tubes; check tube supports allow expansion.
piping: Fuel gas train with double block and bleed, pressure regulation and safety shut-off valves per the burner management system.
Process coil inlet/outlet with flow, pressure and temperature instruments; snuffing steam where required.
commissioning: Refractory dry-out (controlled heating curve); purge; light-off procedure; set excess air (O₂) and draught; verify tube-metal temperatures.

safety: Burner management system with purge, flame detection and fuel shut-offs; never relight without purge.

video_tutorials.title: Gas Fired Furnace — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Gas Fired Furnace.
A gas-fired process heater (furnace) heats a process fluid flowing through tubes.
Burners fire into a refractory-lined radiant box; tubes along the walls absorb radiant heat.
The flue gas then flows up through a convection section, where more tubes recover heat, and leaves by the stack.
Typical applications include crude and vacuum heaters in refineries; reformer and cracking heaters; hot-oil heaters.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Radiant Section Casing & Refractory Lining, Stack (natural draught).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Gas Fired Furnace — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gas Fired Furnace.
Monitor O₂, draught, tube-metal temperatures, flame pattern.
Clean burner tips; check damper.
Inspect tubes (creep, coke) and refractory.
Watch for flame impingement: hot spots, tube bulging. Common cause: burner misalignment, poor air distribution.
Watch for positive pressure at arch: hot gas leaks. Common cause: damper closed too far.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
